apps.title: Hermes Kanban Board
apps.summary: A web-accessible Hermes Kanban operator board with a constrained /api/kanban bridge, live default board data, card management, and high-friction manual execution controls.
safetyPosture: Approved operator writes are enabled on protected app-preview; other deployments may be read-only according to bridge capabilities
No direct Hermes dashboard plugin exposure
operatorChecklist: Open the board and confirm the live or fixture indicator and reported write capabilities; production errors must not substitute demo cards.
Verify backend statuses render, including triage, todo, ready, running, blocked, review, scheduled, done, and any unknown statuses returned by the backend.
Use approved assignment and task-management controls when writes are enabled.
Confirm execution controls are separated into the high-friction panel and ready promotion remains manual.
Use the app-preview surface, not game-preview, for operator use.
nextIdeas: Add execution event streaming and worker process visibility.
Add enrichment-only triage helpers: labels, summaries, dedupe hints, missing-field hints.
Extend the operator app registry as more app-preview tools arrive.

apps.title: Game Dev
apps.summary: A game-development view of Hermes Kanban using the same backend and task store, with game, milestone, and discipline metadata and a manifest-derived game catalog.
apps.testCommand: CI=true KANBAN_MODE=fixture PLAYWRIGHT_PREVIEW_PORT=4315 npx playwright test tests/game-dev-discovery.spec.mjs --workers=1 --output=output/tmp/game-dev-discovery-tests --reporter=list
safetyPosture: A view of the existing Kanban store: no separate board and no new statuses
Approved operator writes follow the same bridge capabilities and protected app-preview access as Kanban
Dispatch/claim remain in the separate high-friction confirmation panel; no automatic ready promotion
Game metadata does not guarantee task/build-linked verification or verified playable builds
operatorChecklist: Open Game Dev from the App Dock on app-preview, not game-preview.
Use the manifest-derived catalog from GET /api/kanban/games to identify a game.
Organize existing tasks with game_dev metadata: game_id, milestone, and discipline; the task store and statuses are unchanged.
Check bridge write capabilities before managing tasks; game previews run separately on game-preview.
nextIdeas: Consider explicit task/build-linked verification as a separately scoped follow-up; it is not guaranteed by this view.
